newsitem.title: USA: Shiva warns of loss, CFO resigns, stock plunges.
newsitem.headline: Shiva warns of loss, CFO resigns, stock plunges.

text.p: Shiva Corp. warned Monday it will report disappointing results for the second quarter in a row and said its chief financial officer had quit, sparking a sharp sell-off of the data equipment maker's stock.
The Bedford, Mass.-based said Cynthia Deysher had resigned as chief financial officer, and has been replaced by Larry Whitman, vice president and corporate controller.
The stock plunged $3.125, or more than 26 percent, to $8.75 on Nasdaq, where it was among the most active issues in late trading.
Shiva, which traded as high as $87.50 in the past year, plummetted on Jan. 8 after it warned that fourth-quarter earnings were likely to be no more than one-third of Wall Street expectations.
Shiva said it expected to take several one-time charges and to incur a substantial operating loss in the first quarter ended March 29. Revenues will fall short of analysts' expectations, it said.
It did not provide specific figures.

Shiva was expected to earn 7 cents per share in the quarter, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates. In the fourth quarter ended Dec. 28, the company earned $1.5 million, or 5 cents a share, on revenues of $48.2 million.
Shiva said sales to end users of its LanRover remote access products fell in the first quarter, largely due to increased price competition.
Shiva said estimated sales for its LanRover Access Switch concentrator also declined in the latest quarter due partly to delays in recognising revenue at several large scale customer installations.

The network equipment maker also cited customer confusion surrounding the new higher-speed 56 kilobit modem technology. Behind the confusion is a battle over a common industry standard for the higher speed Internet access technology.
First quarter results will be reported in the company's regularly scheduled earnings announcement on April 17.
